title: The OSI model: the seven layers and what lives in each one

videos.script: Monday morning, the reception calls. The internet is down. At the next desk, the accountant is working normally, and the website loads on one computer and not on the one beside it. {{call}} The internet is down is not a diagnosis. It is a feeling about a screen. Between that screen and the server that should answer it, there are cables, switches, routers, addresses, ports and programs. Any one of them can be the part that failed. {{between}} The OSI model splits that path into seven layers. Each one uses the layer below it and serves the layer above. For support, its value is practical: it turns one vague complaint into a short list of questions you can answer in order. {{layers}} In this lesson you will look at the layers on a real network: a link and its hardware address, an IP address and a route, a port, and the protocols on top. You will read one packet byte by byte and see which bytes belong to which layer. {{steps}} Then you will break the network four times, once per layer, and learn the message each failure prints. {{break}} The network is a lab: an office, an internet provider and a small internet, built on one computer. That way every command could be run, and every answer is the one it really printed. {{lab}}
